analysis: Documentation-only change in docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md. It updates the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a paragraph after line 783 (head 784-790). The paragraph says provider-staged complete-checkpoint imports create destinations already available from host bytes, with no eval or fence. Staging therefore never waits for MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock, which the engine holds for another request's prefill chunk. It also says the import plan charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch. No source code, policy, crypto, TTL, scope or key handling changed in the supplied evidence. The claimed behavior (CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift) is outside the supplied evidence and is unverified. Relevant threat IDs are T-041 (prefix-cache cross-tenant and TTFT oracle, SSD at-rest), T-028 and T-029 (availability and residual GPU memory), and TB-007. A possible side effect is that skipping eval/fence could alter TTFT or hit-latency behavior. That would be the SEC-035 accepted-risk channel and is not clearly widened. Whether the destination arrays are actually zero-initialised and fully overwritten before use is not verifiable here. The next pass should check the code change that accompanies this doc, if any. It should confirm that host-byte-backed lazy arrays cannot be read before authenticated whole-file validation. It should also confirm that scratch charging stays within the memory reservation ledger. No finding is raised, since a documentation update is not evidence of a regression.
